values.note: Suffolk County's online reservation system, with a Green Key login; on 2026-10-21 the county's Reservations page said a new reservation system is 'coming soon' and some services are temporarily unavailable. Reservations 1 to 180 days ahead (no same-day). From May 15 to Oct 15 a reservation must be at least 4 nights if it takes in Thursday-Sunday and 2 nights if Monday-Wednesday only; 2 nights the rest of the season. A reservation made with the $50 Non-Resident Reservation Green Key must be at least 4 nights at any time ('Non-Resident green key card holders may reserve throughout the season for one week maximum, except the following holiday weeks: Memorial Day ... Fourth of July ... Labor Day'). Sites not reserved go to walk-ups from 8 am, paid in full at check-in, at non-resident rates without a Green Key; the rig must be with you. At most 7 nights, then 7 nights away from that campground. Four people or one family (2 adults and their children) per site.

booking.source: https://www.suffolkcountyny.gov/Departments/Parks/Doing-Business/Rules-and-Regulations/Campground-Rules-and-Regulations (Reservations: 'Reservations will be accepted from 1 to 180 days in advance'; 'Between May 15 and October 15, reservations must be for a minimum of four (4) nights (Thursday - Sunday), and for a minimum of two (2) nights (Monday - Wednesdays only, excluding holidays.) Before May 15 and after Oct. 15, the minimum is two (2) nights'; Check-In: 'Check-in for available walk-up sites will begin at 8:00 am ... Full payment for walk-ups is required at check-in'; Registration: 'Campers must have a valid Green Key Card or pay non-resident rates'; Period of Stay: 'Camping is limited to seven (7) nights maximum. Upon check-out a camper may not return to the same campground for a period of seven (7) nights'; Occupancy: 'four (4) individuals or one (1) single family unit (2 adults and their children)') + https://suffolkcountyny.gov/Departments/Parks/Green-Key-Card ('When making a camping reservation, it requires the user to make a MINIMUM FOUR NIGHTS stay') + https://suffolkcountyny.gov/Departments/Parks/Reservations ('A new Parks Reservation and point-of-sale system is coming soon ... some services are temporarily unavailable'), read 2026-10-21; Sears Bellows' own park page has no reservation-only statement ('Campsites for both tents and trailers are available'; Reservations link -> https://www.reserveparks.suffolkcountyny.gov/), read 2026-10-21

values.note: All 70 family campsites are basic (no electric, outer-beach or full-hookup sites); tent and trailer sites.

note: Suffolk County park on Bellows Pond, Hampton Bays, in the Long Island Pine Barrens. Tent and trailer sites; some sites at the pond. --Claude
summary: County pages: 70 family campsites, all basic (count now verified; no electric, so the note's 'verify hookups; some report primitive' is resolved and electric 0 recorded); open until Veterans Day (closes 11-11; no park-specific opening date); booking block as at Cathedral Pines 1451 (county system with Green Key login, 1-180 days ahead, 2-night minimum / 4 nights Thu-Sun May 15-Oct 15, walk-ups from 8 am at non-resident rates without a Green Key, 7-night max). Sears Bellows' own page has no reservation-only statement, so the walk-up route applies and the entry stays. Fees left as read 2026-10-10. Phone 631-852-8290 confirmed (park General Info). Note: dropped the Green Key, hookup-uncertainty and facilities restatements.
flags: Non-resident access (Indian Island / Smith Point question): no drop. Sears Bellows' park page has no 'Reservations are required for all the sites' statement, and the county Campground Rules give walk-ups ('Check-in for available walk-up sites will begin at 8:00 am ... Full payment for walk-ups is required at check-in'; 'Campers must have a valid Green Key Card or pay non-resident rates'). The Green Key page's 4-night minimum binds only reservations made with the $50 Non-Resident Reservation Green Key. Every reservation needs 2 nights, 4 when it takes in Thu-Sun between May 15 and Oct 15 (in booking.min_stay).

Fees: the entry carries surcharges electric +$8 and sewer +$8 from the county fee schedule, but the county's campsite matrix lists all 70 Sears Bellows sites as basic (no electric or full-hookup sites), so those add-ons never apply here; consider {electric: 0, sewer: 0} or removing them (left alone: fees provenance is a human read).
Household rule (county-wide, as at 1451): a site is limited to 'four (4) individuals or one (1) single family unit'. Not a single-occupancy rule.

The county Reservations page (read 2026-10-21) says 'A new Parks Reservation and point-of-sale system is coming soon'; booking.url may change. Campsite availability on the current WebTrac site shows only after a Green Key login.
